Note the attribute is documented as living on the Vendor Form page; the corpus does not state that page and Vendor Search Admin are the same grid, so treat it as a second location to visit.

sequence.action: add or edit units and set their spend type
sequence.rationale: Reached at Administration > Invoice > Units Of Measure. Units must exist before anything can reference them — the corpus lists three downstream consumers: 'The Unit of Measure field may be added to any of the Item forms (Purchase Request, PO, and Payment Request)', 'The field may be included in PO matching rules and audit rules', and 'The field may be included in a PO or Payment Request import'. Ordering this before Audit Rules (already in the graph) is inference: the corpus states the field may be used in audit rules but does not state a configuration sequence. Values are enumerated: 'Units are associated with a spend type (Goods, Services, or Both).' This page is also open to the Restricted role, unlike most of Group 4.

sequence.action: check Default Goods on the unit that should preselect for Goods items
sequence.rationale: After order 9, because a unit must exist and carry a spend type before it can be the default for that type: 'The administrator can specify a unit type that will always appear as the default choice by checking the box in the Default Goods or Default Services column.' Effect is at item-entry time — 'the default selection for Goods is the one specified as the default in Units of Measure above.'

sequence.action: check Default Services on the unit that should preselect for Services items
sequence.rationale: Parallel control for the other spend type, from the same sentence as order 10. Set both in one pass so Goods and Services do not end up with one defaulted and one not; the corpus notes 'Units of measure appear when a PR item is added and vary depending on the spend type', so a missing default on one type shows up only for that type's users.

configSteps.name: Configure image handling so uploaded and scanned invoices attach and are trackable
configSteps.goal: Create the imaging configuration a policy can consume, allow employee uploads, then add a scan configuration for barcode-tracked paper and bind it to the policy that governs those invoices.

sequence.action: navigate and pick Invoice Imaging or Vendor Imaging
sequence.rationale: Route: 'Click Administration > Invoice (on the sub-menu). Click Image Handling (left menu). The Image Handling window appears.' The tab choice is first and mutually exclusive — the corpus writes it as 'Either: Click the Invoice Imaging tab. – or – Click the Vendor Imaging tab.' The configuration row created next belongs to whichever tab is active, so picking after creating the row is not possible. For vendor-side setup the corpus also names a separate page entirely: '...or, for vendors, Administration > Invoice > Vendor Handling.'

sequence.action: click the default row to edit, or click New for a fresh configuration
sequence.rationale: Step 4 of the procedure, again an either/or: 'Click the default row to edit the existing default configuration. – or – Click New to create a new configuration. A new row appears.' Editing the default silently changes every policy already pointing at it, whereas New leaves existing policies untouched — the writer must decide this before typing a name, not after. Multiple configurations are expected: 'Since a configuration is assigned to a policy, several configurations can be created to be used depending on geographical region, etc.'

sequence.action: enter the configuration Name
sequence.rationale: First field in the row and the one the downstream page consumes: 'Enter a unique name for the configuration. This name will appear as an option when setting up policies.' Uniqueness is required here (unlike scan configuration names), and the name is the only handle the Policies page has on this record.

sequence.action: enter the Acrobat Reader Download URL
sequence.rationale: 'Enter the link to the Adobe Web site where the employee can download the software. The link appears in the error message that displays when the system checks to see if Adobe Reader is installed.' Set before enabling uploads (order 7) because it is the recovery path shown to the employee at the exact moment the check fails — an empty value turns a solvable error into a dead end.

sequence.action: set the Mark invoices received on successful image check checkbox
sequence.rationale: 'Select this check box if you want the system to note the invoices as received when they have transmitted successfully.' Decide it in the same row edit as the other fields, before Save. Bound caveat that should be reflected to the operator: 'NOTE: The employee must verify the clarity and accuracy of the successful transmission of invoices' — the automatic received marking is a transmission signal, not a quality signal.

sequence.action: confirm the accepted file types before opening upload to employees
sequence.rationale: A verification entry, not a settable control — checked before order 7 so the rollout message matches reality. The admin-guides list enumerates TIF, TIFF, JPEG, JPG, PNG, PDF (with XFA; with embedded fonts), Word file (DOC; DOCX), Excel file (XLS; XLSX – not supported: XLTS), EML (File saved using Microsoft Outlook), CSV. Flag the discrepancy rather than reconciling it: the tools-guides sibling topic adds 'CFDi (tax information with PDF)' and drops the XLTS caveat, and a third corpus list covering emails and uploads is narrower still (PNG, JPG, JPEG, PDF, TIF, TIFF, HTML with no double-byte characters).

sequence.action: select Allow employee to upload image files
sequence.rationale: 'Select this check box if you want the Upload Image link to appear to the user in the Actions menu. Doing this allows the employee to click the link and upload images using the Upload Image window.' This is the control that exposes the feature to end users, so it goes after the supporting fields at orders 4-6 are populated. Blocking condition the writer must report rather than work around: 'Note: If this option is not displayed, submit a service request to have this feature turned on.'

sequence.action: click Save on the imaging configuration
sequence.rationale: Procedure step 6, 'Click Save.' Mandatory before any policy work: the umbrella guide orders the whole feature as 'Create an Invoice Imaging Configuration in Administration > Invoice > Image Handling as the Invoice Configuration Administrator' then 'Assign an imaging configuration to a policy in Administration > Invoice > Policies.' An unsaved row does not appear in the Policies list.

sequence.action: record the Upload Image session limit as an operator note, do not attempt to set it
sequence.rationale: Explicitly a read-only runtime constraint on the end-user Upload Image window — a writer that treats it as a numeric admin input will fail looking for a field that does not exist. Bound facts: the limit is 10 files per session, it is repeatable ('To upload more than 10, simple upload the first 10 and then upload another 10, until done'), sessions accumulate ('Multiple sessions can be initiated for a single invoice or vendor request; files are appended to prior uploads for a given invoice'), and the per-file size cap is never stated numerically in the corpus — 'There is a size limit for each image file; the Upload Image window (shown below) displays that limit.' Companion guidance worth passing on: 'When scanning, the images should be scanned at 300 dpi or lower to reduce file size.'

sequence.action: click the Scan Configurations tab
sequence.rationale: Separate sub-feature on the same page, started only after the imaging configuration is saved so the two records are not half-built at once. Corpus route: 'Click Image Handling (left menu). The Image Handling page appears. Click the Scan Configurations tab.' Skip this entire block for sites that do not track paper — scan configuration exists for 'Companies that track paper invoices manually by using barcode technology.'

sequence.action: click New to add a scan configuration row
sequence.rationale: 'Click New. A new row appears ready for input.' The row must exist before its two fields can be typed, and before Policies can offer it at order 15.

sequence.action: enter the Configuration Name
sequence.rationale: 'This is the name of the scan configuration. The name does not need to be unique for each configuration; however, SAP Concur recommends that you use names that are easy to understand and to recognize in the list.' Note the contrast with order 3 — uniqueness is required for the imaging configuration name and explicitly not required here, so name collisions are possible and only the writer's discipline prevents an ambiguous Policies list.

sequence.action: set Image Invoice Container ID Required to Yes or No
sequence.rationale: 'Select Yes or No in the list.' Decide before Save because Yes imposes work on a different role on a different page: 'If Yes, the invoice image processor must populate the Image Invoice Container ID field for invoices associated with this scan configuration on the Process Images page.' Setting Yes without briefing that role stalls image processing.

sequence.action: click Save on the scan configuration
sequence.rationale: 'Click Save. The new configuration appears on the page.' The corpus then states the binding requirement outright: 'Once you have created a scan configuration, you must it assign it to a policy' — so Save is the hinge between this page and order 15, and an unsaved row cannot be assigned.

sequence.action: select the policy, click Modify, and pick the scan configuration
sequence.rationale: Explicit corpus ordering (Step 2 follows Step 1): 'Click Administration > Invoice. Click Policies (left menu)... Select the desired policy. Click Modify... Select the appropriate scan configuration name from the Scan Configuration list. This is the name that you created on the Scan Configuration page in Image Handling.' Cardinality constrains how many times this runs: 'One configuration can be used by multiple policies; however, each policy can only use a single scan configuration.' Assignment is per policy, not per group — 'Scan configuration settings are not based on groups; they are assigned to specific policies.'

sequence.action: select the Timestamp Configuration value if e-Bunsho timestamping is in scope
sequence.rationale: Optional and Japan-specific, and it is NOT an Image Handling control despite belonging to the imaging story — 'On the Administration >Invoice > Policies page, when Invoice Admins modify a policy, the admin will see the Timestamp Configuration field.' Grouped here with order 15 because both are policy-level bindings and the writer is already in Modify Policy. Only one value is named anywhere in the corpus (Japan e-Bunsho); do not assume others. Downstream work continues on Group Configurations (Policies column > Modify > Is Active for Group / Is Default Policy), and image eligibility is physical: 'To be eligible for an e-Bunsho timestamp, images must be more than 200dpi (scanner) or 3.88M pixels (smartphone/digital camera) and at least 24-bit color for RGB.'

sequence.action: open the Exceptions helper pane to add an image-related exception code
sequence.rationale: Last because exceptions describe failures of the pipeline built at orders 1-15 — defining them before the configurations exist means guessing at what can fail. The pane is reachable from inside the Image Handling tool (shared with Audit Rules, Workflows, and Invoice Processor), the alternative entry being 'From within the Exceptions tool'. Visibility gate the writer must check before reporting failure: 'Group administrators can only add exceptions if given create rights for the Invoice Configuration Administrator. If the administrator does not have permissions, the New link does not appear.' The exception attributes themselves are Exceptions-tool fields, not Image Handling fields, and are not configured from this sequence.
